name: September 16, 2025 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 16, 2025
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 RM.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villablanca called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Judy Villablanca; Vice Chair Jake Lingo; Commissioners Alicia Peak
  (arrived at 7:11 p.m.) and Dane Skophammer

  ABSENT: Commissioner Georgia Goldfarb

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Tatiana Holden,
  Assistant Public Works Director; Nathaniel McLean, Assistant Engineer; Chris Orosz,
  Interim Recreation Manager; Niyant Upadhyay, Recreation Coordinator; and Brittany
  Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Villablanca led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Lingo moved, and Commissioner Skophammer seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 3—0;
  Commissioners Goldfarb and Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on September ll, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation on Summer Day Camps by Recreation Coordinator Upadhvav

  Recreation Coordinator Upadhyay provided an overview on 2025 summer day
  camp program offerings, participation, camp locations, and trends.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Tracy Weirick from the Malibu West Beach Club discussed a Coastal Cleanup
  event on September 20, 20257 from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.7 and the Wise and Ready
  Seminar for senior citizens on September 25, 2025, at 12:00 p.m.

  Chair Villablanca closed public comment.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Vice Chair Lingo seconded a motion to
  approve the consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 3-0;
  Commissioners Goldfarb and Peak absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Communitv Services Department Monthlv Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and flle a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in August 2025.

  Commissioner Peak arrived at 7:1 l p.m.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack
  Recommended Action: l) Receive a presentation on the conceptual design of the
  Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack; and 2) Provide feedback to staff regarding the
  design.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report and introduced Jun
  Fujita Hall, Principal Project Architect.

  Ms. Fujita Hall presented three conceptual designs and cost estimates for the Snack
  Shack.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated drainage must be addressed.

  Vice Chair Lingo stated the cost of building the Snack Shack was more than he
  expected. He suggested reducing it to under $4 million. He stated to remove the
  family restroom and add grass rather than decomposed granite to the area
  surrounding the Snack Shack.
   Parks and RecreatiOn Commission

  Chair Villablanca stated to keep the three picnic tables, which are already in place.
  She stated there was no need to add more. She inquired about the kitchen equipment
  and if anything could be taken off the list.

  Ms. Fujita Hall stated she needed the Commission to determine the list of kitchen
  equipment and appliances to calculate the electric load.

  Vice Chair Lingo inquired if a transformer upgrade was required.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated items with a bigger cost like the shade
  structures, picnic tables, and family restroom should be cut rather than cutting
  kitchen equipment since those were smaller expenses.

  Chair Villablanca recommended appointing an Ad Hoc Committee to work with
  staff and the designer on the conceptual design for the Snack Shack.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, Vice Chair Lingo and Commissioner Skophammer were appointed
  to the Snack Shack Ad Hoc Committee to work with staff and the designer on the
  conceptual design of the Snack Shack.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Nathan Hassall Poetry Stone at Legacy Park
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the installation of a poetry stone
  honoring Malibu Poet Laureate Nathan Hassall.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  total budget for the poetry stone, including the etching and installation, was $5,000.

MOTION  Vice Chair Lingo moved, and Chair Villablanca seconded a motion to approve the
  installation of a poetry stone honoring Malibu Poet Laureate Nathan Hassall. The
  question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

  Surf Legend of the Year Award
  Recommended Action: l) Review and provide feedback on the criteria for the Surf
  Legend of the Year Award; and 2) Recommend a 2025 award recipient for City
  Council consideration.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Skophammer recommended changing the name of the award from
  Surf Legend of the Year to be Malibu Surf Legend.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of September 16, 2025
  Page 4 of 5

  Commissioner Peak indicated agreement with Commissioner Skophammer.

  Chair Villablanca recommended opening nominations to the public.

  Commissioner Peak requested to change the award criteria. She stated one person
  should be given the award annually and suggested opening the nomination period
  in February or March and awarding it in June.

  Chair Villablanca stated the timeframe for the award does not need to be specifled.

  Commissioner Skophammer suggested opening public nominations for the 2025
  award to give the public an opportunity to nominate candidates.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated Council provided direction to the Parks
  and Recreation Commission to review the process of creating the award and
  recommending a recipient.

  Chair Villablanca clarified that the Commission recommended the criteria outlined
  in the staff report, with the exception that only one person or group would be
  nominated annually for City Council consideration and approval.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to create the
  Malibu Surf Legend Award with the approved criteria for City Council
  consideration. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Commissioner
  Goldfarb absent.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Chair Villablanca seconded a motion to
  recommend Randall “Crawdaddy” Miod as the 2025 recipient of the Malibu Surf
  Legend Award for City Council consideration. The question was called, and the
  motion carried 4-0; Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Interim Recreation Manager Orosz provided an update on youth sports programs
  and afterschool programs.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on aquatics programs.

  Commissioner Peak stated she had received feedback that the Malibu Marlins
  registration price had increased.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  program costs are set by the instructor, and staff provide instructors with feedback
  and suggestions on prices. She stated the concems would be provided to Recreation
  Manager Manisco for review.

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua provided an update on lap swim passes and
  senior lap swim participants.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on Senior programs,
  Special Events, Equestrian Park, and the Permanent Skate Park.

  ln response to Commissioners Peak and Skophammer, Community Services
  Director Riesgo stated the Park Memorial and Donation program would be placed
  on a future agenda for discussion.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Peak stated that parking at Malibu Bluffs Park on September l3,
  2025, was terrible due to multiple events occurring at Pepperdine University which
  impacted the park. She stated assistance from the Sheriff’s Department was not
  provided.

  Vice Chair Lingo stated that Malibu Little League fall baseball was going well, and
  the opening day for American Youth Soccer Organization (AYSO) also went
  smoothly. He stated his family participated in the Zuma Triathlon and the event
  was great.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Park Memorial Donation Program

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Villablanca adjoumed the meeting at 8:45 p.m.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibu on Novem r l8, 2025.
